pattern.crimePattern: a daughter-in-law who nursed an old man for six years kills him with his own insulin the weekend before he sells the family land, using a key her son had copied
pattern.notes: Fictional family, school trust and house. Teaches the ACCOMPLICE group plainly: the son knowingly had the key cut; the housekeeper lent the spare without knowing why and is refuted by what she knew.

ob.reportedBy: Advocate Simon Maina, for the Ngong Hills Academy Trust
ob.text: An advocate for a school trust reports that his client, Mzee Josiah Kamande (79), died in his sleep at his house in Karen on Saturday night, two days before he was due to sign a land sale. The family doctor was ready to certify natural causes.

facts.text: Mzee Josiah Kamande was found dead in bed in his Karen house on Sunday morning, two days before a land sale; the family doctor was ready to certify natural causes.
Mzee lies in bed, peaceful. His own key is on the bedside table.
The bedroom door was locked when Rehema came with tea at 06:30; she opened it with the spare from her tin. There are only two keys.
Advocate Maina: on Thursday Mzee told him, "If anything happens to me before Monday, look at my family."
On the desk: the sale of 8 acres to the school trust, signing Monday; a trust deed for the grandchildren's education; and a letter to Stephen: "The land has carried your debts long enough."
His insulin pen was new and full on Friday; the dose counter now shows far more than 40 units used.
His logbook: 20 units Friday night and 20 units at 20:00 Saturday. In six years every dose is logged in the stomach.
Alarm log: the corridor sensor outside Mzee's bedroom fired at 23:34 and 23:41. No other internal movement between 22:30 and 05:50.
Alarm log: the perimeter was armed from 22:30 and no outside door opened until 05:50. Rehema's cottage is outside the alarmed building.
Alarm log: the east-wing sensor, outside Stephen's room, never fired after 22:35.
Rehema: "Brian came at about four and asked for the spare key, for Mzee's reading glasses from the drawer. He brought it back before five."
Rehema: "Mzee locked his door because he said a house full of debt is a house full of thieves."
Rehema: at about 22:30 Stephen shouted at his father in the sitting room, "Just sign over two acres to me!", then his room door slammed.
Stephen's club tab closed at 21:55 on Saturday.
Kiosk receipt: Saturday 16:12, one mortice key cut, KSh 600. The cutter remembers "a young man, a Kamande"; the car-park camera shows Brian's car.
Records: Lilian called Brian at 15:40 on Saturday (3 min); Brian paid the key-cutter at 16:14; on Sunday at 07:05 Brian called Lilian (40 s).
In the old stables latrine: a freshly cut mortice key, still bright.
Brian's building gate log: in at 21:00 Saturday, out again at 06:40 Sunday.
Dr. Mbithi chaired a parents' meeting until 21:00 on Saturday, then went home to Langata.
Fingerprints taken from Lilian in detention.
Post-mortem: no heart attack; signs of severe low blood sugar.
Post-mortem: two fresh injection points, one in the stomach and one in the upper left arm, a site he never used.
Post-mortem: death on Sunday between 01:30 and 04:00.
Lab: a very high insulin concentration at the arm site, far above the rest of the body.
Lab: the latrine key was cut on the kiosk's machine from the same brand of blank, and it opens the bedroom lock.
Lab: Mzee's prints on the pen, and a partial of Lilian's on the dose knob. She handles his medicines every day.
Lilian: "I went to bed at ten and didn't leave my room all night. Stephen came in drunk and went to bed."
Lilian: "I've washed that old man, fed him, counted his tablets for six years. And on Monday he would give the land to strangers' children."
Lilian: "I have never had a key to his room. Only Mzee and Rehema."
Brian: "I never touched Grandpa's key. I was in Westlands all afternoon."
Brian: "Mum asked me to get a copy. She said one day he'd fall behind that door. On Sunday morning she called and said 'throw it away'. I threw it in the old latrine. I knew then."
Stephen: "I was at my club until one in the morning."
Stephen: "I came home at half past ten and begged him for two acres. He said no. I went to my room and drank. I didn't go near him after that."
Rehema: "I lent the key to Brian for the glasses and he brought it back."
Dr. Mbithi: "His death kills the sale. The trust gains nothing from it."

interrogations.intro: Lilian sits on the sofa with his medicine box on her knees, tired and gentle. "I went to bed at ten and didn't leave my room all night. Stephen came in drunk and went to bed."
Brian keeps his hood up in his mother's sitting room. "I never touched Grandpa's key. I was in Westlands all afternoon."
Stephen hasn't slept. "I was at my club until one in the morning."
Rehema answers before you finish asking. "I lent the key to Brian for the glasses and he brought it back."
Dr. Mbithi drives over from Langata. "His death kills the sale. The trust gains nothing from it."
Advocate Maina waits in the hall with his hat in his hands.

reconstruction.text: Mzee Kamande plans to sell 8 of his 12 acres to a school trust on Monday and put the money into his grandchildren's education. Stephen will keep the house but not the land he has borrowed against for years.
Saturday, 15:40. Lilian calls Brian. At four he borrows Rehema's spare "for Grandpa's glasses", has a copy cut at the Karen kiosk at 16:12, and returns the original before five.
At 20:00 Mzee gives himself his evening dose in the stomach and logs it. At 22:30 Stephen comes home drunk, shouts for two acres, and goes to his room.
At 23:34 Lilian lets herself into the bedroom with the copy while he sleeps and injects a large dose from his own pen into his upper arm. At 23:41 she locks the door behind her.
He dies between half past one and four. At 07:05 Brian calls his mother. She says "throw it away", and he drops the key into the old stables latrine.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Brian and a warrant on the outbuildings. The insulin assay (18 h) goes with the body first thing; detain Lilian after the latrine search; the key comparison (8 h) and prints (6 h) come back inside 24 h.

ui.beatNotes: The second sentence. When the WHO group is filled, a second line slides out beneath it on the charge sheet: "…helped by ____, who ____." The first time, Mwalimu calls, unprompted, her first hint call in weeks: "Most people who kill don't do it alone, Amani. Find who held the door."
